checks_performed: Read only the specified source input and draft; used no web or other source files.
Compared the exact target against the draft's claimed resolution and final writeup.
Reconstructed all sixteen arguments, checking antiparallel cases, ceiling inequalities, quantifiers, reductions, disjoint-set counts, and applicability of the quoted rainbow-girth results.

Ran an exact integer/Boolean checker for the small-order claims. It checked 25 triangle-free oriented graphs on three vertices, 19,940 candidate indegree vectors, 12,800 local n=10 arc patterns, and all 45 parameter pairs with 2<=n<=10.

claims.claim: Tail-color reduction: if D has no antiparallel pair, form an undirected graph whose edge {v,w} has color v whenever v→w. Every rainbow cycle in this graph is a directed cycle of D of the same length.
claims.evidence: On a rainbow cycle of length l, all l colors are distinct and each is the tail endpoint of its edge. They therefore equal the l cycle vertices, each exactly once. Thus every vertex has exactly one outgoing edge on the oriented cycle. An orientation of an undirected cycle with outdegree one at every vertex is consistently directed, giving a directed l-cycle.
claims.search_method: Direct reconstruction of the orientation argument, including uniqueness of each edge color from absence of antiparallel arcs.

claims.evidence: Selecting one outgoing arc at every vertex produces a finite functional digraph. Iteration repeats a vertex within n+1 terms, and the segment between consecutive occurrences is a directed cycle of length at most n=ceil(n/1).

An antiparallel pair gives a 2-cycle, which meets the bound. Otherwise retain exactly two outgoing arcs per vertex. The tail-colored graph has n disjoint color classes of size two. The supplied Theorem 1 with p=0 gives a rainbow cycle of length at most ceil(n/2), and claim 0 transfers it to D.
claims.search_method: Case split on antiparallel arcs followed by exact matching of the tail-colored graph to supplied Theorem 1.

claims.evidence: Without an antiparallel pair there are at most n(n-1)/2 arcs, while minimum outdegree d gives at least nd>=n^2/2, a contradiction. Hence a directed 2-cycle exists. Since d<=n-1 and d>=n/2, ceil(n/d)=2.
claims.search_method: Exact arc count and ceiling check.

claims.claim: Every such D has a directed cycle of length at most n-d+1.
claims.evidence: For a longest simple directed path v1→...→vm, every outneighbor of vm lies earlier on the path. The largest index j among at least d such outneighbors satisfies j>=d. The arc vm→vj closes a cycle of length m-j+1<=n-d+1.
claims.search_method: Longest-directed-path proof with the indexing inequality checked directly.

claims.claim: There is a universal C<=10^11 such that every D has directed girth at most Cn/d.
claims.evidence: The supplied source states the corresponding rainbow-girth theorem with a universal C0<=10^11. Without antiparallel arcs, retaining d outgoing arcs at each vertex yields n tail-color classes of size d, so claim 0 transfers the rainbow bound. With an antiparallel pair, girth is two; replacing C0 by max(C0,2) preserves the stated upper limit and gives 2<=Cn/d because d<n.
claims.search_method: Checked the hypotheses of the supplied universal rainbow-girth result under the tail-color reduction, including the omitted antiparallel case.

claims.claim: For each fixed d there is a constant alpha_d>0 such that every D has directed girth at most n/d+alpha_d.
claims.evidence: The supplied source states the additive rainbow-girth bound n/d+alpha_d for n color classes of size d. Claim 0 transfers it when there is no antiparallel pair. If an antiparallel pair exists, enlarge alpha_d to at least one; then 2<=n/d+alpha_d since n>d.
claims.search_method: Checked the supplied additive rainbow theorem's hypotheses and separately handled antiparallel arcs.

claims.claim: If a counterexample exists, one of minimum order can be taken oriented, strongly connected, and exactly d-outregular; moreover d>=3 and K=ceil(n/d)>=3.
claims.evidence: A counterexample has no antiparallel pair because ceil(n/d)>=2. Deleting excess outgoing arcs preserves counterexample status and makes every outdegree exactly d. A sink strongly connected component retains all d outgoing arcs; if proper, it is a smaller counterexample because ceil(|S|/d)<=ceil(n/d). Global minimality therefore makes the graph strongly connected. Claims 1–3 exclude d<=2 and K<=2.
claims.search_method: Minimal-counterexample reduction with deletion monotonicity and sink-component order checked explicitly.

claims.claim: In a minimum-order counterexample, every outneighborhood S has minimum internal outdegree at most ceil(d/K)-1.
claims.evidence: Exact d-outregularity gives |S|=d<n. If the internal minimum outdegree is r>=1, minimality applies the target to D[S], producing a cycle of length at most ceil(d/r). Since the counterexample has no cycle of length at most K, ceil(d/r)>K, equivalently d/r>K. Hence r<d/K and, integrally, r<=ceil(d/K)-1. For r=0 the bound is immediate.
claims.search_method: Direct minimality argument with the ceiling equivalence checked exactly.

claims.claim: Every minimum-order counterexample satisfies n>=3d+2-ceil(d/K). In particular, when K=3 it satisfies 3d+2-ceil(d/3)<=n<=3d.
claims.evidence: Choose v with indegree at least d and u∈N+(v) with at most ceil(d/K)-1 internal outneighbors. At least d-ceil(d/K)+1 outneighbors of u lie outside N+(v). They avoid v and N-(v), since otherwise there is respectively a directed 2- or 3-cycle. Thus {v}, N+(v), N-(v), and those extra outneighbors are disjoint, yielding n>=1+d+d+d-ceil(d/K)+1. If K=3, ceil(n/d)=3 also gives n<=3d.
claims.search_method: Reconstructed the disjoint-set count and checked both short-cycle exclusions and the K=3 ceiling implication.

claims.claim: If n<=2d+ceil((d+1)/2), then D has a directed cycle of length at most 3.
claims.evidence: Assume no 2- or 3-cycle and trim to exact outdegree d. Choose v with indegree at least d. The oriented graph on S=N+(v) has average internal outdegree at most (d-1)/2, so some u has at most floor((d-1)/2). Its at least ceil((d+1)/2) remaining outneighbors avoid v and N-(v), or create a 2- or 3-cycle. The resulting disjoint sets force n>=1+2d+ceil((d+1)/2), contradicting the hypothesis.
claims.search_method: Exact averaging and disjoint-set count, including the parity identity d-floor((d-1)/2)=ceil((d+1)/2).

claims.claim: For d=3 and n<=9, D has a directed cycle of length at most 3.
claims.evidence: With no short cycle, every three-vertex outneighborhood has an internal sink u. The sets {v}, N+(v), N+(u), and N-(v) are disjoint, so n>=7+d-(v). For n<=9 this makes every indegree at most two, contradicting average indegree three after trimming. The exact checker verified the sink property in all 25 triangle-free oriented three-vertex patterns and enumerated all 19,940 degree vectors allowed by the inequality.
claims.search_method: Direct proof plus exhaustive integer/Boolean enumeration of the local orientations and all permitted indegree vectors for 2<=n<=9.

claims.claim: For d=3 and n=10, D has a directed cycle of length at most 4.
claims.evidence: The preceding count makes a putative counterexample 3-in/3-out regular. For fixed v, partition the other vertices into S=N+(v), I=N-(v), and three nonneighbors R. Short cycles forbid S→I. If every R vertex receives from S, then 4-cycles forbid R→I, leaving each I vertex at most two possible inneighbors. Otherwise some r0∈R receives nothing from S. The nine arcs leaving S then require at least six S→R arcs; the other two R vertices admit at most six, forcing a transitive tournament on S, whose sink must send to all three R vertices, including r0. The checker exhaustively examined all 12,800 triangle-free internal-S and S→R patterns: all 163 locally degree-feasible patterns covered every R vertex, and none had an uncovered R vertex.
claims.search_method: Direct partition proof plus exhaustive Boolean enumeration of every relevant local arc configuration.

claims.claim: The target holds for semicomplete digraphs.
claims.evidence: An antiparallel pair gives the required 2-cycle. Otherwise the digraph is a tournament. Minimum outdegree at least one rules out a transitive tournament, so a directed cycle exists; a shortest tournament cycle is a triangle by examining the chord between its first and third vertices. Finally d<=(n-1)/2 implies ceil(n/d)>=3.
claims.search_method: Case split followed by the standard shortest-cycle chord argument and an exact average-degree bound.

claims.claim: The target holds for every n<=10.
claims.evidence: Claims 1 and 2 cover d<=2; claim 3 covers 2d>=n; claims 11 and 12 cover the remaining d=3 cases; and claim 10 covers the only remaining possibilities, d=4 with n=9 or 10. The exact checker enumerated all 45 pairs 2<=n<=10 and 1<=d<n and confirmed that each falls under at least one of these proved cases.
claims.search_method: Exact enumeration of every admissible integer pair (n,d), backed by the verified component lemmas.

claims.claim: For every 1<=d<n, the circulant digraph on Z_n with arcs i→i+s mod n for 1<=s<=d has directed girth exactly ceil(n/d).
claims.evidence: For any directed cycle, its positive step sizes lie in {1,...,d} and sum to a positive multiple of n, so a cycle of length l satisfies ld>=n and l>=ceil(n/d). Let L=ceil(n/d). The increments d repeated L-1 times followed by n-(L-1)d all lie in {1,...,d}, sum to n, and have distinct proper partial sums strictly between 0 and n. They therefore form a simple directed L-cycle.
claims.search_method: Exact modular-increment lower bound and explicit cycle construction.
claims.witness: For arbitrary 1<=d<n, use the cycle from 0 with increments d,...,d,n-(ceil(n/d)-1)d.

target_evidence: The exact target requires either a proof of the Caccetta–Häggkvist bound for every admissible digraph or an explicit counterexample whose girth exceeds it. The draft explicitly claims only PARTIAL resolution and supplies correct special cases, approximation bounds, minimal-counterexample restrictions, and a sharpness construction. It supplies neither a universal proof nor a counterexample, so it makes material but incomplete progress: VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS. Because claimed_resolution is PARTIAL and the final writeup expressly disclaims a full proof or counterexample, that resolution label is ACCURATE rather than overstated or understated.
